title: Roxy-WI <= 8.2.6.4 — Unauthenticated Root RCE (?api=1 auth bypass -> /scheduler/jobs os.system)

exposure.note: Roxy-WI web interface. The advisory demonstrates the attack on port 8080; deployments also front it on 8443/443. The vulnerable routes are the flask_apscheduler /scheduler/* API plus the whitelisted /static/* read-back, reachable unauthenticated by appending ?api=1.

affected_technologies.note: The advisory lists 'Patched versions: None'. Verified at source: the described bug (app/login.py:19 `if 'api' not in request.url`) is present verbatim at the v8.2.6.4 tag. The master branch has already replaced it with a proper endpoint allow-list + JWT validation, so current master is NOT vulnerable to the described bypass; the advisory's cited master commit 7744ecf5f53955f3c0036ddd52f539930ef24b36 already contains the hardened code. The repo documents Roxy-WI 9.1+/Helm 10.1.0, newer than the affected range. Confirm the running version against 8.2.6.4 rather than assuming all deployments are affected.

preconditions: A Roxy-WI instance at or below 8.2.6.4 (code containing app/login.py:19 substring auth check) reachable over HTTP(S).
Default configuration: SCHEDULER_API_ENABLED=True with no SCHEDULER_AUTH, flask_apscheduler started (app/__init__.py). These are the shipped defaults.

unverified.cve_mapping: GHSA-hqf9-xcvr-7xj5 has no CVE in its CVE field; the auth-bypass root cause is attributed to CVE-2026-45567 in the advisory body. The RCE-chain advisory itself is tracked here by its GHSA id. Treat the CVE association as asserted, not confirmed from NVD (NVD was not machine-readable at build time).
unverified.fixed_version: No fixed release is named. The bypass is absent on current master, but the exact first-fixed release/tag was not established.

log_monitoring_urls.query_or_body: any request whose URL query string contains 'api' (e.g. ?api=1), with a JSON body containing "func":"os:system" (or os:popen, subprocess:*, builtins:*, nt:system)
log_monitoring_urls.reason: Registration of an OS-command job through the unauthenticated scheduler API is the core exploit step.
Synchronous trigger of a scheduler job without authentication — the execution step.

log_monitoring_urls.query_or_body: URL contains 'api' and references a file that is not a normal static asset (e.g. rwi_*.txt, *_id.txt, *_shadow.txt)
log_monitoring_urls.reason: Read-back of command output written into the whitelisted static directory.

request_body_signatures: Any authenticated-looking action reached with 'api' in the query string on a non-API route (the bypass primitive): e.g. GET/POST .../scheduler/...?api=1, ...?x=api.
A /scheduler/jobs body with "func" set to a dangerous callable reference such as os:system, os:popen, subprocess:run, subprocess:Popen, builtins:exec, builtins:eval, nt:system, posix:system.
behavioral: Scheduler jobs whose func is not one of the application's own app.jobs:* functions.
Files appearing under the app static directory that are command output (id/whoami/shadow dumps) rather than assets.
New cron entries, authorized_keys additions, or outbound connections from the Roxy-WI host shortly after /scheduler/jobs activity.
flask_apscheduler executing a job immediately after a /run call from an unauthenticated session.

remediation.primary: Upgrade Roxy-WI to a build whose app/login.py uses the endpoint allow-list + JWT validation (current master / 9.x+) instead of the `if 'api' not in request.url` substring check.
steps: Update Roxy-WI to the latest release (the repo documents 9.1+ and Helm chart 10.1.0). Confirm app/login.py no longer contains `'api' not in request.url` and that /scheduler/* requires authentication.
Treat any instance that ran <= 8.2.6.4 as compromised: it allowed unauthenticated root command execution. Investigate for planted cron jobs, SSH authorized_keys, new users, and modified binaries.

Rotate all secrets reachable from the host: the Roxy-WI JWT keys (/var/lib/roxy-wi/keys/*), DB credentials, managed HAProxy/Nginx/Keepalived host SSH keys and passwords, and rotate OS credentials since /etc/shadow was readable.
If the scheduler API is not needed, set SCHEDULER_API_ENABLED=False (or configure SCHEDULER_AUTH) so the /scheduler/* routes are not exposed.
Review web/access logs for 'api' appearing in query strings on non-API routes and for POSTs to /scheduler/jobs and /scheduler/jobs/*/run.
mitigations_if_upgrade_impossible: At the reverse proxy / WAF, block requests that carry an 'api' token in the query string on non-API paths, and block all external access to /scheduler/* and to /static/* requests that reference non-asset filenames.
Disable the scheduler API (SCHEDULER_API_ENABLED=False) or require SCHEDULER_AUTH.
Restrict network access to the Roxy-WI interface to trusted management hosts only; never expose it to untrusted networks.
Run the Roxy-WI process as a non-root, least-privilege account to reduce blast radius.

signatures.description: The auth-bypass primitive: an 'api' substring anywhere in the query string of a non-API route. Primary signal is any ?api= / =api on /scheduler/* or /static/*.
A scheduler job whose func resolves to an OS-command / code-exec callable (os:system, subprocess:run, builtins:exec, ...). No legitimate dashboard job uses these.
Synchronous job trigger. Combined with the ?api bypass this is the execution step; block/alert when reached without an authenticated session.

waf.combine: block any request to /scheduler/* or /static/* whose query string contains an 'api' token (the bypass), and independently block any /scheduler/jobs body whose func targets os/subprocess/builtins/etc.
waf.false_positive_notes: Roxy-WI's legitimate frontend reaches the scheduler through the authenticated, blueprinted API, not by sprinkling 'api' into the query string of /scheduler or /static routes, so blocking that pattern on those paths is safe. Dangerous func prefixes (os:, subprocess:, builtins:, ...) are never used by the application's own jobs (app.jobs:*).
